question: In January 2025, a camera trap in Namdapha Tiger Reserve captured an elephant after 12 years, indicating the presence of elephants in which Indian state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Namdapha Tiger Reserve is located in the Changlang district of **Arunachal Pradesh**, India.
 
• In January 2025, a camera trap in the reserve captured an elephant, marking the first sighting in the area after 12 years.
 
• This sighting confirms the presence of elephants in the northeastern state of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The reserve is renowned for its rich biodiversity, housing species like tigers, leopards, and red pandas, alongside elephants.
 
• Namdapha Tiger Reserve is an important ecological hotspot and part of the larger Indo-Burma biodiversity region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Namdapha Tiger Reserve:** Established in 1983, it is the largest protected area in Arunachal Pradesh and the third largest national park in India.
 
• **Elephant Habitat:** Elephants in Arunachal Pradesh are part of the northeastern population, which is known for its migratory behavior across borders with neighboring states and countries.
 
• **Indo-Burma Biodiversity Hotspot:** Namdapha lies within this globally recognized region, known for its high levels of endemism and species diversity.
 
• **Camera Traps in Wildlife Conservation:** These are remote, motion-activated cameras used to monitor wildlife presence and behavior in dense forests and other hard-to-access areas.
 
• **Conservation Challenges:** The presence of elephants in Namdapha highlights the need for habitat protection, anti-poaching efforts, and mitigation of human-wildlife conflict in Arunachal Pradesh.
